newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian communists oppose Tata-SIA linkup.
newsitem.headline: Indian communists oppose Tata-SIA linkup.

text.p: The Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M) on Tuesday urged Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet to reject a proposed joint airline venture between Tata Industries Ltd and Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA).

The CPI-M politburo said in a statement that the joint venture, cleared by the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB) of senior government officials, would mark a major departure from the government policy.
Earlier on Tuesdday, newspapers said the FIPB had recently approved the controversial $600 million venture and sent it to the Cabinet Committee on Foreign Investment for a final decision.
A senior government official later confirmed the reports.

The CPI-M said it was surprising the FIPB had cleared the proposed joint venture to set up a domestic airline as it was at odds with Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim's position that foreign participation in domestic airlines would not be permitted.
It said the venture would also contradict the view of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Civil Aviation which had studied the question.

"The Politburo of the CPI-M wishes to draw the attention of the government that this joint venture would be a major departure from the policy so far adopted not to allow foreign investment into the domestic airlines sector," it said.
"There is no reason whatsoever for this policy to be changed. The Politburo requests the union cabinet not to reverse this stand," it said.
The Financial Express on Tuesday quoted Ibrahim as saying a new civil aviation policy being drafted by the government would bar foreign firms from taking an equity stake in domestic airlines.
The CPI-M backs Deve Gowda's 13-party centre-left coalition government, but is not represented in the cabinet.
